source.anchor: Official C2S programme call page: startup/MSME participation, project categories, proposal route, evaluation and call-window history

conditions: applicant must fit the current C2S project category and notified call
startup/MSME status is determined under the extant DPIIT or Ministry of MSME norms
project must state technical novelty, deliverables, targeted TRL, fabrication/testing or prototype plan and commercialization or technology-transfer roadmap as applicable
collaborative proposals must define nodal institution, roles, financial requirements, timelines and applicable MoUs
academic institutions must meet the infrastructure, faculty, accreditation and student-project conditions applicable to their category
the applicant must submit through the current official C2S route and proposal format

thresholds.startup_and_msme_definition: extant DPIIT or Ministry of MSME norms

benefit.label: C2S call-specific project support with EDA/fabrication access

summary.summary: Call-specific project support plus EDA, fabrication and design-infrastructure access for eligible C2S participants; no generic applicant amount is established by the reviewed umbrella pages.

application.route: Verify the current C2S call or support route, select the applicable project category, prepare the prescribed technical and financial proposal with supporting documents, register/login on the official portal and submit through the notified route.
application.selection: Proposal scrutiny and evaluation by the applicable Evaluation or Review Committee; approval and support depend on the current call, category, budget, milestones and notified terms.

requirements.name: Current C2S call/category fit with technical proposal, institutional or startup/MSME evidence and applicable collaboration, infrastructure, milestone and reporting documents
requirements.description: Prepare the current prescribed proposal, applicant-status evidence, technical novelty and deliverables, targeted TRL, EDA/fabrication/testing plan, commercialization or technology-transfer roadmap, team and collaborator details, budget/contribution, MoU or end-user letter where applicable, and supporting certificates as required by the current category.

steps.title: Verify the current C2S call or support route
steps.description: Check the official C2S call pages and resources for an open startup/MSME, academic/R&D, RSC, EDA or other notified route; do not rely on a historical call date.

steps.title: Classify the applicant and project category
steps.description: Confirm startup/MSME or academic/R&D eligibility, project category, semiconductor-design scope, existing infrastructure, CI/Co-CI and collaborator requirements.

steps.title: Prepare the technical and financial proposal
steps.description: Use the current prescribed format and assemble novelty, TRL, deliverables, EDA/fabrication/testing, commercialization, budget, contribution, supporting certificates and collaboration documents.

steps.title: Submit through the official C2S route and track milestones
steps.description: Register or log in on the official portal, submit the notified proposal and retain evaluation, approval, agreement, milestone, PFMS, utilization, IP and reporting records.

window.label: Paused: historical C2S calls are visible, the BLDC call is marked closed and the RSC call deadline was 22 July 2026; no current general C2S call was verified on 8 September 2026.

evidence.anchor: Official BLDC call page states proposal submission is closed; the official RSC page records a 22 July 2026 deadline, while the programme page records the historical 15 September 2023 second-call deadline.

finePrint.milestone_release: The guidelines state that milestone-linked fund releases apply to participating institutions under the approved project.
finePrint.infrastructure: No separate funds are provided for creation of new facilities under the general guidelines; existing infrastructure and category-specific support conditions apply.
finePrint.accountability: Participating institutions must maintain project, PFMS, reporting, inventory, IP and utilization records as applicable to the current category and agreement.
finePrint.ip: IP sharing among collaborators follows the mutually agreed terms included in the proposal and applicable programme conditions.
finePrint.current_portal_state: The official portal currently shows a historical second C2S call with a 15 September 2023 deadline, a BLDC Motor Controller ASIC call marked closed, and an RSC call with a 22 July 2026 deadline. No currently open general C2S call was verified on 8 September 2026.
finePrint.window_note: Keep the umbrella record paused until a current startup/MSME or institution-facing call is verified; create separate component records if a new call has materially different eligibility, benefit, deadline or application terms.
finePrint.review_note: Reconcile the active project category, current call, budget or support ceiling, applicant boundary, proposal format, evaluation, milestones, fund release, fabrication, EDA access, PFMS, IP, reporting, audit and grievance terms before publication.

records.name: GEN-NEXT Support for Innovative Startups (GENESIS)
records.authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology - GENESIS

source.anchor: Introduction, eligibility, major components and detailed documents

conditions: the startup or ecosystem entity must fit the current component and implementing-agency route
the support route is component-specific and may require an eligible incubator, accelerator or selected implementing agency
startup location, technology, stage, selection, diligence, matching and pilot evidence must be verified for the relevant call
a scheme outlay or aggregate ecosystem target is not an individual applicant entitlement
exclusions: a startup treating the GENESIS scheme outlay as a guaranteed grant
an applicant outside the current component, implementing agency, geography or selection process
investment or pilot support presented without component-specific diligence, matching or milestone conditions
a startup using historical brochure ceilings without confirming the current call or agency route

benefit.label: GENESIS component-specific pilot, investment and deep-tech support

summary.summary: Component-specific startup ecosystem support through selected implementing agencies, including possible pilot, early-stage, investment or deep-tech routes. The scheme budget is not an applicant benefit and values must not be combined across components.

application.route: Identify the current GENESIS component and selected implementing agency, then follow the agency's official call, application and diligence route
application.selection: Component-specific screening, expert selection, technical/commercial diligence, agency approval, milestones and monitoring

requirements.name: Technology startup or eligible ecosystem entity with a component-fit proposal
requirements.description: Prepare incorporation and startup-recognition evidence, location and technology-stage proof, product or pilot plan, team, traction, budget, IP, diligence and matching/investment evidence required by the selected component and agency.

steps.title: Select the current GENESIS component
steps.description: Determine whether the need is ideation, pilot, early-stage, investment, deep-tech or ecosystem/incubator support and confirm the current official component route.

steps.title: Identify the selected implementing agency
steps.description: Verify the current agency, geography, startup stage, application window, diligence list and support instrument before preparing the proposal.

steps.title: Submit and complete diligence
steps.description: Use the agency's official call route, submit the component-specific proposal and retain selection, investment, pilot, milestone and reporting evidence.

window.label: GENESIS opportunities are component- and implementing-agency-specific; no universal national deadline or direct applicant entitlement is asserted.

evidence.anchor: Major components and list of selected implementing agencies

finePrint.scope: The official pages describe GENESIS as an umbrella scheme with Tier-II/III-focused support and components including Entrepreneur in Residence, pilot funding, investment support and deep-tech funding.
finePrint.funding: The official brochure describes historical component boundaries including early-stage support up to Rs. 10 lakh, pilot support up to Rs. 50 lakh, deep-tech support up to Rs. 1 crore and investment support up to Rs. 50 lakh with private-sector matching; these are component-specific references, not a universal grant or loan ceiling.
finePrint.route: MeitY Startup Hub implements the ecosystem through selected implementing agencies; the startup-facing route, geography, stage, matching, selection and current availability must be checked for the active call.
finePrint.review_note: Confirm the current GENESIS component, selected agency, active call, geographic and stage criteria, support instrument, matching or investment terms, diligence documents, milestones, reporting and whether historical component ceilings remain current.

records.name: Reimbursement of Testing and Certification Charges for Telecom Start-ups and MSEs
records.authority: Department of Telecommunications - Telecom Engineering Centre

source.anchor: Overview, reimbursement criteria, scheme duration and application portal

conditions: the applicant must be a telecom start-up or MSE satisfying the current scheme route
testing or certification must be carried out at a TEC/NCCS-designated or recognized lab or an eligible NABL-accredited lab where applicable
the applicant must provide the required incorporation, financial, registration, lab, report, invoice, payment and bank evidence
the same testing and certification charges must not already have been reimbursed under another Government scheme
exclusions: testing or certification charges outside the eligible telecom product and laboratory route
a business without DPIIT start-up or Udyam evidence where required
expenses already reimbursed under another Government scheme
claims that exceed the entity-level cap, fund availability, eligible percentage or current application period
applications missing invoices, payment receipts, test reports, product certificates, financials or required declarations

benefit.label: Telecom testing and certification charge reimbursement

summary.summary: Partial reimbursement of eligible telecom testing and certification charges at entity-category-specific rates, subject to evidence, no-double-benefit, fund and duration limits. This is not an advance grant or universal subsidy.

application.route: Submit the online reimbursement application with the incorporation, DPIIT/Udyam, financial, laboratory, test report, product certificate, invoice, payment, bank and declaration documents
application.selection: Document and eligibility review by the implementing route; reimbursement depends on eligible charges, evidence, fund availability and applicable cap

requirements.name: Eligible telecom start-up or MSE with completed testing/certification evidence
requirements.description: Prepare incorporation, DPIIT or Udyam, audited financial, eligible-lab, test-report/product-certificate, invoice, payment, bank, PAN and no-duplicate-reimbursement evidence, plus the required revenue and funding declarations.

steps.title: Confirm applicant and product eligibility
steps.description: Verify the telecom-sector route, DPIIT/Udyam status, entity category, revenue/funding declarations and eligible product or certification scope.

steps.title: Use an eligible laboratory and retain evidence
steps.description: Confirm TEC/NCCS designation or eligible NABL accreditation, complete testing/certification and retain reports, product certificates, invoices and payment receipts.

steps.title: Submit the reimbursement claim
steps.description: Submit online through the TEC portal while the current scheme period and funds remain available; retain the application and acknowledgement.

window.label: The official page states a two-year implementation period or earlier closure when the Rs. 25 crore allocation is exhausted. Confirm the implementation date, remaining funds and any extension before showing an actionable deadline.

evidence.anchor: Scheme Duration and application portal

finePrint.rates: The official page states reimbursement of 75% for start-ups, 60% for micro enterprises and 50% for small enterprises, subject to the scheme rules and entity-level cap.
finePrint.cap: The official page states a maximum reimbursement of Rs. 50 lakh per entity and a Rs. 25 crore allocation boundary; exhaustion of funds or the scheme duration can end availability earlier.
finePrint.duration: The official page states the scheme operates for two years from implementation or until the allocated funds are fully utilized, whichever is earlier. The current implementation date, remaining funds and any extension require verification.
finePrint.documents: The official guideline requires incorporation, audited financial statements, DPIIT or Udyam registration, eligible laboratory evidence, test reports/product certificate, invoices, payment receipt, bank details, PAN and declarations including no duplicate reimbursement; it also states revenue and prior-funding conditions that require applicant evidence.
finePrint.review_note: Confirm current portal acceptance, implementation date, remaining fund balance, laboratory list, product/certification scope, entity-size test, revenue and funding thresholds, eligible cost period and any amendment before publication.

records.name: PM E-DRIVE: EV Public Charging Station deployment support
records.authority: Ministry of Heavy Industries (MoHI)

source.anchor: Pages 1-4, Questions 1-13: location categories, benchmark charger costs, eligible proposal entities, nodal-agency route, CPO selection, commissioning, uptime, data sharing and recovery conditions

conditions: proposal must be submitted by an eligible Government or public-sector entity through the appointed nodal agency route
the nodal agency must aggregate demand and submit the EV PCS proposal to the Ministry of Heavy Industries
each proposed location must have a feasibility study covering location selection, configuration and charger rating
locations must provide unrestricted public access
the implementing agency must commission, maintain and monitor the chargers and share required location, availability, pricing and payment data with the designated national hub
a private Charge Point Operator may be appointed only through the nodal agency's fair and transparent selection process
exclusions: ordinary founders, startups, private landowners and private CPOs are not direct subsidy beneficiaries under the EV PCS FAQ
the subsidy is provided only to the appointed nodal agency; a CPO is an implementation/procurement route, not automatically the subsidy recipient
charger benchmark values are not a universal per-applicant grant ceiling and upstream infrastructure depends on DISCOM demand notes and appraisal
refundable deposits and GST are not eligible subsidy costs
a proposal may be accepted or rejected by the Ministry of Heavy Industries and excess subsidy can be recovered with interest if location categorisation is wrong
the total scheme outlay is a programme cap, not an individual entitlement
the scheme and its components are fund-limited and component-specific amendments or exhausted funds can close a route before the terminal date

benefit.label: EV public-charging station subsidy through an appointed nodal agency

summary.summary: Proposal-based EV charging-infrastructure subsidy routed through appointed Government/public-sector nodal agencies, with separate deployment, commissioning, data and maintenance obligations; no direct founder entitlement is asserted.

application.route: An eligible Government or public-sector entity appoints or acts through a nodal agency, aggregates demand, completes feasibility and location documentation, submits the EV PCS proposal to the Ministry of Heavy Industries, and then follows the approved deployment, commissioning, data and maintenance route.
application.selection: Ministry of Heavy Industries evaluation of the nodal-agency proposal; revised proposals may be evaluated first-come, first-served, while the Ministry retains acceptance/rejection discretion.

requirements.name: Eligible institutional applicant, appointed nodal agency, feasible public locations and approved EV PCS proposal
requirements.description: Prepare institutional authority, nodal-agency appointment, demand aggregation, location access, feasibility, charger configuration, DISCOM, procurement, commissioning, maintenance and data-sharing evidence under the current EV PCS guideline.

steps.title: Confirm institutional and nodal-agency eligibility
steps.description: Verify that the applicant is an eligible Government/public-sector entity and identify the appointed nodal agency; ordinary private CPOs should not be treated as direct beneficiaries.

steps.title: Aggregate demand and complete feasibility
steps.description: Prepare location, public-access, configuration, charger-rating, demand, DISCOM and implementation evidence for each proposed EV PCS site.

steps.title: Submit through the Ministry route
steps.description: The appointed nodal agency submits the proposal to the Ministry of Heavy Industries and retains the acceptance, rejection or clarification record.

steps.title: Procure, commission and operate
steps.description: Follow the approved procurement/CPO route, energise and commission the chargers, maintain uptime and share required data with the designated national hub.

window.label: Institutional proposal route under current EV PCS guidelines; no universal public founder application window is asserted.

evidence.anchor: Current guideline index lists EV PCS operational guidelines and a December 2025 EV PCS FAQ; confirm current proposal intake with the appointed nodal agency.

finePrint.location_categories: The FAQ distinguishes Category A and Category B locations and requires unrestricted public access; the responsible nodal agency decides categorisation under the operational guidelines.
finePrint.benchmark_costs: The September 2025 FAQ lists benchmark charger costs including INR 1.60 lakh for 12kW LEVDC/LECCS, INR 3.40 lakh for 60kW CCS-II, INR 5 lakh for 120kW, INR 8 lakh for 240kW and INR 12.50 lakh for 360kW, all including GST as displayed; refundable deposits and GST are not eligible subsidy costs, so the calculation needs reconciliation before publication.
finePrint.upstream_infrastructure: Upstream infrastructure subsidy is based on DISCOM demand notes or estimates and abnormally high costs may be excluded.
finePrint.commissioning: The final tranche for eligible advance-subsidy cases is tied to energisation, commissioning and onboarding to the proposed Unified Bharat E-Charge hub.
finePrint.operations: Implementing agencies must maintain high uptime and share charger location, availability, pricing and digital-payment data.
finePrint.scheme_period: The Gazette extension states an overall PM E-DRIVE period through 31 March 2028 and a total outlay of INR 10,900 crore; component-specific terminal dates and amendments must be reconciled from the current notification index.
finePrint.review_note: Before publication, reconcile the controlling EV PCS operational guideline, latest MHI amendment, nodal-agency proposal window, benchmark-cost treatment, subsidy percentages/caps, eligible-location categories, DISCOM evidence, CPO procurement route, commissioning milestone, data hub status and any 2026 amendment.

records.name: Incentive Scheme for Production of Foreign Films in India and Official Co-productions
records.authority: India Cine Hub - Foreign Film Incentive

source.anchor: Incentive Calculator: up to 40% support, production categories, fee, documents and application processing notes

conditions: Project must fit an eligible production or official co-production category under the current guideline
Qualifying production expenditure must be incurred in India
Foreign production applicants use an Indian line producer or production services company where required
The project must pass the portal's script/content and permission review
For the additional manpower bonus, at least 15% Indian cast/crew manpower must be evidenced where the guideline applies
For the Significant Indian Content bonus, the project must satisfy expert script evaluation
exclusions: The current India Cine Hub calculator says it does not accept documentary films, audio-visual commercials or music videos for this online route
An official co-production must satisfy the applicable bilateral audio-visual co-production agreement
The additional manpower and Significant Indian Content bonuses are conditional and must not be assumed
The portal's incentive estimate is not a sanction or guarantee of reimbursement
Local, monument, forest, railway, animal and other location permissions may still be required separately

benefit.label: Up to 40% reimbursement of qualifying production expenditure in India, subject to guideline conditions and cap

amounts.label: Significant Indian Content bonus where applicable

summary.summary: Up to 40% of qualifying production expenditure incurred in India, combining a base reimbursement and conditional bonuses, subject to the official guideline and an indexed INR 30 crore cap; do not present the percentage as a guaranteed payout.

application.route: Register on India Cine Hub, submit the international production or official co-production application, pay the non-refundable INR equivalent of USD 225 processing fee, provide the script/synopsis and required production documents, complete permission review, and use the verified incentive claim route through the Indian production services company or other eligible applicant.
application.selection: Ministry of Information and Broadcasting/India Cine Hub review includes script evaluation and permission checks; incentive eligibility and payout remain subject to the governing guideline and approval.

requirements.name: Eligible international production or official co-production, India-incurred qualifying expenditure, Indian production services/line-producer arrangement where applicable, script and production permissions, and evidence for any claimed manpower or Significant Indian Content bonus
requirements.description: Prepare the script and synopsis, crew passport table and copies, Indian locations and shoot period, temporary-import equipment list, applicable NOC, official co-production agreement, expenditure evidence, Indian manpower evidence and Significant Indian Content material. Confirm the current claim form and claimant boundary before submission.

steps.title: Confirm project category and current guideline
steps.description: Check that the proposed production is accepted by the current India Cine Hub route and verify the latest incentive guideline, claimant and cap.

steps.title: Register and prepare the permission dossier
steps.description: Register on India Cine Hub and prepare the script or concept, crew passports, locations, dates, equipment and applicable NOC or co-production agreement.

steps.title: Submit the application and processing fee
steps.description: Submit through the official portal and pay the non-refundable INR equivalent of USD 225 processing fee. Treat the fee separately from any approved reimbursement.

steps.title: Track permission and incentive claim readiness
steps.description: Track script review, permission, local permits, qualifying expenditure, Indian manpower/SIC evidence and the verified post-production claim route; do not treat the calculator estimate as approval.

window.label: Official India Cine Hub online route is currently presented as available; verify the latest guideline and live incentive-claim intake before handoff.

evidence.anchor: Current Incentive Calculator page, last updated 04 September 2026, with online application fee and production-category prompts.

finePrint.scope: The scheme supports international film production projects and official audio-visual co-productions with qualifying expenditure in India, including live production and certain animation, post-production and VFX services subject to the current guideline.
finePrint.benefit: The current official calculator presents up to 40% of qualifying spend in India. Indexed official guideline material describes a base reimbursement up to 30% of Indian qualifying production expenditure, with an additional 5% for at least 15% Indian manpower in applicable live-shoot projects and an additional 5% for Significant Indian Content.
finePrint.cap: Indexed official guideline material states an enhanced incentive payout cap of INR 30 crore. The cap and the claimant/entity treatment must be confirmed against the latest accessible guideline before publication.
finePrint.processing: The current international-project guide says permission normally takes no more than three weeks after all requisite documents are submitted, with longer processing where Ministry of Home Affairs or Ministry of External Affairs consultation is required.
finePrint.documents: Detailed script and synopsis or reality-show concept, crew passport details, Indian shooting locations and period, temporary-import equipment list, applicable no-objection letter, and official co-production agreement where relevant.
finePrint.review_note: Before publication, verify the latest guideline file, cap, eligible project categories, claimant, qualifying-expenditure definition, claim timing, bonus evidence, current portal handoff and whether the route is accepting new applications.

records.name: NMDFC Term Loan Scheme for Employment-Generating Ventures
records.authority: National Minorities Development and Finance Corporation - Term Loan Scheme

source.anchor: Term Loan Scheme: notified minority communities, Credit Line 1/2 income limits, loan ceilings, interest, moratorium and repayment

conditions: applicant must belong to a notified minority community: Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Parsi or Jain
Credit Line 1 applies to annual family income up to INR 3 lakh and Credit Line 2 applies to annual family income up to INR 8 lakh, subject to current policy confirmation
venture must be commercially viable and technically feasible under the selected route
application and appraisal are handled through State Channelizing Agencies or banking partners
credit line, project cost, beneficiary contribution, interest, moratorium and repayment terms must be selected and verified separately
women beneficiaries may receive the stated Credit Line 2 rate concession subject to current terms

benefit.label: Track-specific NMDFC term credit: up to INR 20 lakh (Credit Line 1) or INR 30 lakh (Credit Line 2)

summary.summary: Track-specific concessional term credit for viable employment-generating ventures: current NMDFC pages describe up to INR 20 lakh under Credit Line 1 and up to INR 30 lakh under Credit Line 2, subject to income, project, contribution and SCA conditions.

application.route: Confirm the applicable credit line, prepare minority, income, residence, KYC and project evidence, and apply through the relevant State Channelizing Agency or banking partner.
application.selection: The SCA or banking partner verifies eligibility, project viability, contribution, documentation and repayment capacity; UdyamVeda cannot approve or disburse the loan.

requirements.name: Minority certificate, income/residence/KYC evidence and viable project documents
requirements.description: Provide self-attested income certificate, residence proof, minority/religious certificate, identity/KYC records, project report where required, cost estimates, contribution evidence and SCA/bank forms.

steps.title: Select the correct NMDFC credit line
steps.description: Check annual family income, women-beneficiary concession, project cost and current Credit Line 1/2 terms without combining the ceilings.

steps.title: Prepare minority and project documents
steps.description: Collect income, residence, minority, KYC, project, cost and contribution evidence required by the current SCA or bank.

steps.title: Apply through the channel partner
steps.description: Submit through the relevant State Channelizing Agency or banking partner and complete its appraisal and documentation process.

steps.title: Complete disbursement and repayment setup
steps.description: Confirm the final sanction, interest, contribution, moratorium, utilization period, repayment schedule and post-disbursement obligations.

window.label: Rolling channel-finance route; local SCA/banking-partner availability and current policy must be confirmed.

evidence.anchor: Current scheme page describes standing Term Loan Scheme terms and does not state a single nationwide closing date.

finePrint.credit_lines: The current NMDFC schemes page describes Credit Line 1 up to INR 3 lakh annual family income with up to INR 20 lakh credit at 6% p.a., and Credit Line 2 up to INR 8 lakh annual family income with up to INR 30 lakh credit at 8% p.a. for male beneficiaries and 6% p.a. for women beneficiaries; the current policy and SCA terms must be reconciled.
finePrint.funding_pattern: The official pages describe an NMDFC:SCA:beneficiary pattern of 90:5:5 and a minimum beneficiary contribution, while the Credit Line 1 detail describes up to 90% of project cost and a minimum 5% beneficiary contribution; show these as funding conditions, not extra benefits.
finePrint.repayment: The current summary states a 6-month moratorium and 5-year beneficiary repayment period; confirm the current agreement, utilization period and SCA repayment terms.
finePrint.route: Applications are routed through State Channelizing Agencies and banking partners, not treated as a direct public NMDFC checkout flow.
finePrint.review_note: Human review must reconcile the current NMDFC scheme page, FAQ, Credit Line 1 detail, lending policy, current forms, SCA availability, project-cost rule, contribution, security, interest, moratorium, repayment and amendments before publication.

records.name: NMDFC Micro-Finance Scheme for Minority SHGs
records.authority: National Minorities Development and Finance Corporation - Micro-Finance Scheme

source.anchor: Micro-Finance Scheme: SHG members, minority women focus, Credit Line 1/2 member and group ceilings, interest and repayment

conditions: beneficiary must belong to a notified minority community under the selected current credit line
beneficiaries must be organized into an eligible SHG and satisfy thrift, credit and SCA requirements
Credit Line 1 and Credit Line 2 have different income, member-level, group-level, interest and repayment terms
the route is implemented through State Channelizing Agencies and current SHG/partner rules
women-focused and minority-composition conditions must be verified against the current guideline and SCA

benefit.label: NMDFC SHG micro-credit with separate member and group ceilings by credit line

summary.summary: Track-specific SHG micro-credit: current NMDFC pages describe member and group ceilings under two credit lines, with separate rates and women-focused concessions; no personal or group sanction is guaranteed.

application.route: Form or join an eligible Self Help Group, complete thrift/credit and minority/income documentation, and apply through the relevant State Channelizing Agency under its current micro-finance process.
application.selection: The SHG, SCA and implementing partners verify group/member eligibility, project/activity and repayment structure; UdyamVeda cannot sanction or disburse credit.

requirements.name: Eligible SHG, minority and income evidence, thrift/credit records and viable micro-activity information
requirements.description: Provide SHG/member records, minority and income certificates, KYC, residence proof, thrift/credit information, activity/project details and current SCA forms or declarations.

steps.title: Confirm SHG and current credit line
steps.description: Verify group composition, member eligibility, income line, member/group ceiling and women concession under the current guideline.

steps.title: Prepare group and member records
steps.description: Collect SHG formation, thrift/credit, minority, income, residence, KYC and activity evidence.

steps.title: Apply through the SCA
steps.description: Submit the SHG route through the relevant State Channelizing Agency and follow its current appraisal and documentation process.

steps.title: Complete disbursement and repayment setup
steps.description: Confirm member/group sanction, rate, contribution, moratorium if any, repayment and monitoring obligations before accepting funds.

window.label: Rolling SCA-led micro-finance route; no single nationwide closing date is stated in the reviewed sources.

evidence.anchor: Current page describes a standing Micro-Finance Scheme implemented through SCAs.

finePrint.structure: The current NMDFC page describes micro-credit to SHG members, especially minority women, through SCAs; group formation and thrift/credit discipline are part of the route.
finePrint.credit_lines: Current summary values are up to INR 1 lakh per member and INR 20 lakh for a group under Credit Line 1, and up to INR 1.5 lakh per member and INR 30 lakh for a group under Credit Line 2, with separate rates and women concessions.
finePrint.repayment: The current summary states a 3-year repayment period; current SCA agreement and guideline terms must be confirmed.
finePrint.review_note: Human review must confirm the current micro-finance guideline, SHG size/composition, income line, member/group ceiling, interest, women concession, thrift, SCA route, documents, repayment and amendments before publication.

steps.title: Complete disbursement and repayment setup

records.name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Drones and Drone Components (Closed)
records.authority: Ministry of Civil Aviation - Drone PLI

source.anchor: Eligibility, turnover thresholds, FY 2021-22 to FY 2023-24 tenure, 20% rate, 40% value addition, outlay and per-manufacturer cap

conditions: applicant must be a company registered in India and manufacture qualifying drones or drone components
eligible products include drones, airframes, propulsion, power systems, batteries, navigation, control, communication, cameras, sensors, spraying/payload and safety components; the list may change
Indian MSME/startup annual sales turnover threshold was INR 2 crore for drones and INR 0.5 crore for components
Indian non-MSME annual sales turnover threshold was INR 4 crore for drones and INR 1 crore for components
component manufacturer must establish that the component is used solely in drone manufacturing

components not established as used solely in drone manufacturing
duplicate benefits or submissions contrary to the scheme and PMA review

treating the ₹9 crore project ceiling or scheme corpus as an automatic entitlement

steps.description: Confirm the project DPR, at least 2 TPD capacity, 50% agricultural-residue feedstock, applicable physical progress and GOBARdhan registration.

steps.title: Complete procurement and verification
steps.description: After approval, procure from an authorised OEM/dealer, upload invoices and equipment identifiers, support physical verification and apply for release of assistance.

window.label: Quarterly intake; the guideline states 30 September 2026 as the last date for applications unless extended. Verify the EIL BAM portal for the currently open window before recommending.

evidence.anchor: Guideline paragraphs 5.1-5.2, especially quarterly intake and last date

finePrint.assistance: Maximum assistance is 50% of BAM procurement cost or INR 90 lakh per set, whichever is lower. The guideline describes INR 1.8 crore for a 4 TPD project with a pro-rata cap of INR 9 crore per project.
finePrint.timing: Applications are accepted quarterly from the 1st to the 30th day of the quarter; the revised guideline states 30 September 2026 as the last date or an extension date, but the official EIL BAM portal observed on 8 September 2026 displayed a 1 July to 30 July 2026 intake notice. The current window is unresolved and must not be presented as actionable.
finePrint.procurement: Approval must precede procurement. After approval, the producer purchases from an OEM or authorised dealer, uploads invoices, payment proof, equipment identifiers and photographs, and undergoes physical verification.
finePrint.documents: The guideline lists a DPR, financing or self-finance declaration, GOBARdhan certificate, non-duplication undertaking, plant photographs/geocoordinates, relevant CTO/PESO or plan/consent documents, machinery quotation and bank details.
finePrint.obligations: The beneficiary signs a five-year bond, primarily uses BAM for CBG biomass collection, maintains and insures eligible equipment above INR 5 lakh, files annual biomass-collection reports and may face recovery, benefit suspension or transfer consequences for misuse or non-compliance.
finePrint.review_note: Human review must confirm the currently open quarterly window, revised guideline version, approved machinery list, PMA/CNA route, portal availability, current documents, budget availability and any extension before publication.

records.name: Yuva Sahakar - Cooperative Enterprise Support and Innovation Scheme

the society has operated for at least three months
the society has positive net worth
the society satisfies the applicable cash-loss, project-viability, contribution, security and NCDC appraisal conditions
the project activity and any proposed subsidy or convergence fit the current NCDC and implementing-scheme rules

benefit.label: Yuva Sahakar cooperative innovation project finance

application.route: Prepare a viable cooperative project and apply through the current NCDC financing/application route, directly or through the applicable State Government/UT channel.

requirements.name: Eligible cooperative and viable innovation project
requirements.description: Provide cooperative registration, operation period, net-worth and loss history, innovation/value-chain project report, cost and working-capital split, contribution/debt-equity, security, financials and any convergence evidence requested by NCDC.

steps.title: Confirm cooperative eligibility
steps.description: Verify cooperative registration, at least three months of operation, positive net worth and applicable cash-loss history.

steps.title: Classify the innovation project
steps.description: Document the new, innovative or value-chain-enhancement activity and map it to an eligible cooperative business sector.

steps.title: Calculate project finance
steps.description: Separate project cost, working capital, contribution, debt-equity, project-cost band, security and repayment assumptions; keep working capital within the applicable cap.

steps.title: Prepare appraisal and convergence evidence
steps.description: Prepare the business plan, financials, estimates, member and governance records, security and any separately approved subsidy or convergence documents.

steps.title: Use the official NCDC route
steps.description: Apply through the current NCDC or State Government/UT route and retain sanction, loan, repayment, interest-incentive, monitoring and grievance records.

window.label: Yuva Sahakar is a framework-based NCDC financing route; current application forms, rates, channel and acceptance availability must be confirmed before action.

evidence.anchor: Current NCDC scheme and financing navigation; framework availability does not itself establish sanction or an open application call

interest_incentive.condition: valid only for timely repayments and subject to the applicable NCDC rate/circular

debt_equity_patterns.category_a: 80:20 for eligible cooperatives in the North Eastern Region, Aspirational Districts, or with 100% women, SC, ST or PwD members, subject to current criteria

finePrint.security: Mortgage, FDR, credible cooperative/government/statutory/financial-institution guarantee or other security may be required to NCDC's satisfaction.
finePrint.subsidy: Subsidy from a flagship Government scheme or another source may apply only if the proposed activity is separately eligible; Yuva Sahakar itself is not a guaranteed subsidy.
finePrint.review_note: Confirm the latest NCDC scheme/circular, current rate, project-cost and working-capital limits, three-month operation test, cash-loss test, Category A preference, debt-equity, security, direct versus State route, subsidy convergence, appraisal, repayment, monitoring and grievance terms before publication.
